THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONTAINS INSIDE INFORMATION AS DEFINED IN ARTICLE 7 OF REGULATION (EU) NO 596/2014 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL OF 16 APRIL 2014 ON MARKET ABUSE (MARKET ABUSE REGULATION) AS RETAINED AS PART OF UK LAW BY VIRTUE OF THE EUROPEAN UNION (WITHDRAWAL) ACT 2018 AS AMENDED.
Cardiff, UK
21 July 2026
Trading Update
-
H1 performance ahead of expectations, driven by InP demand for AI and data centre applications
-
Uplift in FY 2026 revenue guidance to in excess of 30% growth year-on-year
IQE plc (AIM: IQE, "IQE" or the "Group"),
the leading global supplier of compound semiconductor wafer products and advanced material solutions
, today provides a trading update for the six months ended 30 June 2026.
Trading in H1 2026 exceeded management expectations with strong demand across all of the Group's core segments, which is expected to result in first half revenue of at least £64m.
Demand for IQE's Indium Phosphide (InP) solutions is continuing to accelerate due to their critical role in enabling optical photonics products for data centres and AI infrastructure. Revenue growth was also supported by ongoing strength in aerospace and defence segments, as well as robust demand for both 3D sensing and wireless products.
This momentum is expected to continue throughout 2026, and as a result IQE now expects FY 2026 revenue growth in excess of 30% year-on-year, resulting in low-teens £m adjusted EBITDA.
The Group remains bank-debt free with a cash position as at 30 June 2026 of £41.6m.
Jutta Meier, Chief Executive Officer of IQE, commented:
"I am very pleased that H1 trading exceeded our expectations. Our long-established leadership in InP and other key material systems means we are critically embedded in supply chains enabling industry trends that will continue to deliver further progress in H2. I remain extremely excited about the significant opportunities ahead for the transformed IQE, and look forward to sharing our continued progress."

company_30s.what_they_do: IQE plc builds and sells silicon‑based photonic devices used in high‑speed data centres and AI accelerators. They make laser chips, optical transceivers and related components that let computers move data faster.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The world is moving to 5G, cloud and AI, all of which need more optical bandwidth. IQE’s chips are a critical link in that supply chain, and their technology is used by major data‑centre operators and semiconductor giants.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is still generating modest revenue and is working on scaling production. Cash burn is moderate, and the company is actively seeking orders to support growth. The stock trades at a low price relative to its peers, suggesting a steep discount to its intrinsic value.

rns_narrative: IQE is preparing for its upcoming results and has announced a £14 m AI‑related order that could boost short‑term sales.
The company has signed a supply agreement with Tower Semiconductor, which should help secure a steady stream of InP wafers for its production lines.
Corporate updates include new director appointments, a notice of results and a trading update, signalling the company is keeping its governance in order while focusing on growth.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Cautiously optimistic—investors are waiting for the AI order to materialise.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Some traders see the AI contract and the Tower deal as a clear upside catalyst that could lift the stock to the middle of its 52‑week range.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Others point to the sector’s recent sell‑off and worry that the company’s cash burn could outpace revenue growth.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The mood has shifted from flat to mildly bullish after the AI order announcement, but the overall chatter remains thin.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for IQE is essentially flat, meaning the market is not yet aware of any impending catalyst.

near_term_catalysts: The results announcement on 12 Aug 2026 could reveal whether the AI order has already begun generating revenue.
If the company reports an earnings beat or a higher-than‑expected order intake, volume should spike and the price may start to climb.
A clear price move back toward the 0.05 p support level would confirm that the bottom is holding.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sustained 20‑day volume surge and a breakout above the 0.05 p support. Earnings that beat consensus or a new large order would also be a green flag.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early recovery phase of a deep crash. Confirmation of mean reversion will likely come with the earnings release or a volume‑backed breakout.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the stock rebounds to 50 % of its 52‑week high, the upside would be roughly 35 % of the current price, while the risk is limited to the 70 % drop that brought it to its present level. The AI order and supply agreement are tangible catalysts that could trigger the bounce.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: Sector volatility and the company’s ongoing cash burn could keep the price stuck below the 0.05 p support. A missed earnings target or a slowdown in AI demand would extend the decline.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Risk is about 70 % of the 52‑week high; reward is about 35 % of that high. The asymmetry is roughly a 1:0.5 risk‑to‑reward ratio.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the stock closes above 0.06 p on a 20‑day volume spike. Allocate 10 % of the account, set a stop 10 % below the entry, and trail the stop as the price climbs.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until the earnings release or until the AI order is confirmed in the results. Watch for a breakout above the 0.05 p support and a 20‑day moving‑average crossover.
playbook.if_passing: There are no immediate delisting or bankruptcy risks, so a bearish exit is not required at this stage.

ai_insights.bottom_line: IQE’s deep price drop coupled with a promising AI contract offers a modest upside if the market reverts, but the lack of a clear signal and sector risk keep the trade speculative.
